A cake is a block that can serve as food. It can be eaten by placing and using it, with each use consuming one of its seven slices. The entire cake gives the most hunger points out of every food item, but has low saturation.
A cake with candle is an uneaten cake with any type of candle placed on it, which can be lit with a flint and steel to emit light.
entities.name: Cake with Brown Candle

entities.blurb: Carpets are thin variants of wool that can be dyed in any of the 16 colors.
entities.name: Brown Carpet

entities.blurb: Concrete is a block created when concrete powder touches water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: Brown Concrete

entities.blurb: Concrete powder is a gravity-affected block that is converted to concrete when touching water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: Brown Concrete Powder

entities.blurb: Glazed terracotta is a vibrant solid block that comes in the sixteen regular dye colors, obtained by smelting stained terracotta. Glazed terracotta does not stick to slime blocks or honey blocks, and it cannot be pulled by sticky pistons, but it can be pushed by pistons.
entities.name: Brown Glazed Terracotta

entities.blurb: A brown mushroom is a fungus found in the Overworld and the Nether. It can only be planted in mycelium, nylium, podzol, or darkness, which also allows it to spread over time or receive bone meal to grow into a huge brown mushroom.
entities.name: Brown Mushroom

entities.blurb: A mushroom block is a solid block that makes up a huge mushroom, which consists of a mushroom stem and brown mushroom blocks or red mushroom blocks, depending on the color of the huge mushroom.
entities.name: Brown Mushroom Block

entities.blurb: A shulker box is a dyeable block that stores items, and, unlike all other storage blocks, keeps its contents in item form when broken.
entities.name: Brown Shulker Box

entities.blurb: Stained glass is a dyed variant of the glass block.
entities.name: Brown Stained Glass

entities.blurb: A stained glass pane is a dyed version of a glass pane. It is a transparent block that can be used as a more efficient alternative to stained glass blocks.
entities.name: Brown Stained Glass Pane

entities.blurb: Stained terracotta is a dyed variant of terracotta obtained by crafting undyed terracotta with dyes. Some of the variants are found in badlands biomes, and all variants can be smelted into glazed terracotta.
entities.name: Brown Terracotta

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: Brown Wall Banner

entities.blurb: Wool is a block obtained from sheep that can be dyed in any of the sixteen different colors. It can be used as a crafting material and to block vibrations.
entities.name: Brown Wool

entities.blurb: A bubble column is an air-providing vertical water current. It is created by magma blocks and soul sand and, depending on the block used, will either pull entities downward or push them upward, respectively.
entities.name: Bubble Column

entities.blurb: Coral is a type of non-solid block that comes in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn. Each of them are vibrant and colorful, but turn gray when they die.
entities.name: Bubble Coral

entities.blurb: A coral block is a solid block that comes in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
entities.name: Bubble Coral Block

entities.blurb: Coral fans are non-solid blocks that come in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
entities.name: Bubble Coral Fan

entities.blurb: Coral fans are non-solid blocks that come in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
entities.name: Bubble Coral Wall Fan

entities.blurb: Budding amethyst is a fragile block found in amethyst geodes that grows amethyst clusters over time. It drops nothing if it breaks, and cannot be moved from where it is found.
entities.name: Budding Amethyst

entities.blurb: A bush is a non-solid plant block found in many grassy biomes. Its color is biome-dependent, and matches the color of grass blocks.
entities.name: Bush

entities.blurb: A cactus is a plant block found in deserts and badlands. It grows over time and can sprout cactus flowers. It damages mobs and destroys minecarts and dropped items that touch it.
entities.name: Cactus

entities.blurb: A cactus flower is a type of flower that grows from cacti. It can be placed on any solid top surface or crafted into pink dye.
entities.name: Cactus Flower

entities.blurb:
A cake is a block that can serve as food. It can be eaten by placing and using it, with each use consuming one of its seven slices. The entire cake gives the most hunger points out of every food item, but has low saturation.
A cake with candle is an uneaten cake with any type of candle placed on it, which can be lit with a flint and steel to emit light.
entities.name: Cake

entities.blurb: Calcite is a block exclusively found in geodes and stony peaks.
entities.name: Calcite

entities.blurb: A calibrated sculk sensor is a craftable type of sculk sensor that functions similarly, but detects vibrations more quickly and from further away. Its amethyst-covered input side can be powered to make the sensor only detect vibrations from specific sources, depending on the signal strength used. Placing an amethyst block next to a sculk sensor allows it to "relay" detected vibrations to other sculk sensors.
entities.name: Calibrated Sculk Sensor

entities.blurb: A campfire is a block that can be used to cook food, pacify bees, or act as a spread-proof light source, a smoke signal, or a damaging trap.
entities.name: Campfire

entities.blurb:
A candle is a dyable block that emits light when lit with a flint and steel. Up to four of the same color of candle can be placed in one block space, which affects the amount of light produced.
Dyed candles are the dyed variants of candles that come in all sixteen colors. Once dyed, they cannot be changed into a different color.
entities.name: Candle

entities.blurb:
A cake is a block that can serve as food. It can be eaten by placing and using it, with each use consuming one of its seven slices. The entire cake gives the most hunger points out of every food item, but has low saturation.
A cake with candle is an uneaten cake with any type of candle placed on it, which can be lit with a flint and steel to emit light.
entities.name: Cake with Candle

entities.blurb:
A carrot is a food item obtained from carrot crops that can be used to plant them, eaten, or used as a crafting ingredient.
Carrot crops are planted in farmland and used to grow carrots.
entities.name: Carrots

entities.blurb: A cartography table is a utility block used for cloning, zooming out, and locking maps. It also serves as a cartographer's job site block.
entities.name: Cartography Table

entities.blurb: A carved pumpkin is a block obtained by using shears on a pumpkin. It is used to craft jack o'lanterns, build golems, and can be worn as a helmet.
entities.name: Carved Pumpkin

entities.blurb: A cauldron is a block that can contain water, lava, or powder snow and, in certain situations, collect them from the environment. In Bedrock Edition, it can also hold dyed water or potions and can be used to efficiently create tipped arrows. It also serves as a leatherworker's job site block.
entities.name: Cauldron

entities.blurb:
Air is an invisible block used to define unoccupied space where other blocks and items could exist; it represents the absence of a block or an item. It is one of the few blocks in the game that players cannot normally interact with.
Cave air‌[Java Edition  only] is a variant found only underground in carver caves[verify for Java Edition] and some generated structures along with features like lava lakes.
Void air‌[Java Edition  only] is a variant used internally for the 'air' in unloaded chunks and outside of the world height limits (above Y=319 and below Y=-64 in the Overworld, and above Y=255 and below Y=0 in the Nether and the End dimensions).
entities.name: Cave Air

entities.blurb:
Glow berries are a food item obtained from cave vines and can be used to plant them.
Cave vines are a climbable plant that hangs off ceilings and grows glow berries. Cave vines with glow berries produce light.
entities.name: Cave Vines

entities.blurb:
Glow berries are a food item obtained from cave vines and can be used to plant them.
Cave vines are a climbable plant that hangs off ceilings and grows glow berries. Cave vines with glow berries produce light.
entities.name: Cave Vines Plant

entities.blurb:
A command block is an indestructible block that can execute commands. Because it cannot be obtained, destroyed or used in Survival mode without cheats, it is primarily used in multiplayer servers, Creative worlds, and custom maps. There are 3 types of these blocks.
An impulse command block is the default block type; it executes only once when activated.
A chain command block executes every time when triggered.
A repeating command block executes every game tick as long as it is activated.
entities.name: Chain Command Block

entities.blurb: A wooden button is a type of button that remains pressed for longer than a stone button and can additionally be pressed by arrows and thrown tridents.
entities.name: Cherry Button

entities.blurb: The wooden door is a variant of the door made of wood that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Cherry Door

entities.blurb: A wooden fence is the wooden variant of fences, crafted using planks and sticks.
entities.name: Cherry Fence

entities.blurb: A fence gate is a block that shares the functions of both the door and the fence.
entities.name: Cherry Fence Gate

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Cherry Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: Leaves are transparent blocks that generate as part of trees and are sources of their respective saplings. They dissipate over time when not attached to logs, but persist when placed by players. Falling-leaf particles occasionally drop from leaves.
entities.name: Cherry Leaves

entities.blurb: A log or stem is a naturally occurring block found in trees or huge fungi, primarily used as a building block and to create planks, a versatile crafting ingredient. There are currently nine types of logs: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, and pale oak; and two types of stems: crimson and warped. The upcoming third drop of 2026 introduces poplar as the tenth log type.
entities.name: Cherry Log

entities.blurb: Planks are common blocks used as building blocks and in crafting recipes. They are usually one of the first things that a player crafts in Survival mode. There are currently 12​[until: Third Drop 2026]/13​[upcoming: Third Drop 2026] variants of planks, which can be differentiated into three categories: Overworld planks made from tree logs, bamboo planks made from blocks of bamboo, and nonflammable Nether planks made from huge fungus stems.
entities.name: Cherry Planks

entities.blurb: A wooden pressure plate is a wooden variant of the pressure plate. It can detect all entities, producing the maximum signal strength of 15. Wooden pressure plates come in all variants of wood.
entities.name: Cherry Pressure Plate

entities.blurb: A sapling is a non-solid block that can be grown into a tree.
entities.name: Cherry Sapling

entities.blurb:
A shelf is a block that can store and display up to three stacks of items. Using an item slot exchanges its contents with the player's hotbar. Powering a shelf combines its three slots together and makes using it swap everything at once.
Two or three adjacent shelves can merge their slots together if all are powered, which allows for swapping six or nine items at a time, respectively.
entities.name: Cherry Shelf

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Cherry Sign

entities.blurb: A wooden slab is a wooden variant of a slab crafted from its respective planks.
entities.name: Cherry Slab

entities.blurb: Wooden stairs are a wooden variant of stairs, crafted from their respective planks.
entities.name: Cherry Stairs

entities.blurb: A wooden trapdoor is a variant of the trapdoor that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Cherry Trapdoor

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Cherry Wall Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Cherry Wall Sign

entities.blurb: Wood or hyphae is a block that has the log's "bark" texture on all six sides. It comes in 11 types (12 in Third Drop 2026​[upcoming]): oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, crimson, warped, pale oak, and poplar​[upcoming].
entities.name: Cherry Wood

entities.blurb:
A chest is a block used to store items.
A large chest (or "double chest") is the combination of two adjacent chests, and can store twice as many items.
entities.name: Chest

entities.blurb: An anvil is a gravity-affected utility block used to rename items, combine enchantments and repair items without losing the enchantments. An anvil has limited durability, and as it is used or dropped too far, gradually becomes a chipped anvil, then a damaged anvil, then breaks and disappears, without dropping anything in return.
entities.name: Chipped Anvil

entities.blurb: Chiseled bookshelves are blocks that can hold books, books and quills, written books, enchanted books, and knowledge books.
entities.name: Chiseled Bookshelf

entities.blurb: Chiseled cinnabar is a decorative chiseled variant of cinnabar used for building.
entities.name: Chiseled Cinnabar

entities.blurb: Chiseled copper is a variant of copper blocks that generates in trial chambers.
entities.name: Chiseled Copper

entities.blurb: Chiseled deepslate is a variant of deepslate. The block depicts a generic face not specific to any mob.
entities.name: Chiseled Deepslate

entities.blurb: Chiseled Nether bricks are a decorative variant of Nether bricks, crafted from Nether brick slabs.
entities.name: Chiseled Nether Bricks

entities.blurb: Chiseled polished blackstone is the chiseled variation of polished blackstone. It has a piglin nose figure.
entities.name: Chiseled Polished Blackstone

entities.blurb: A chiseled quartz block is a variant of the block of quartz that can be crafted from quartz slabs.
entities.name: Chiseled Quartz Block

entities.blurb: Chiseled red sandstone is the chiseled variant of red sandstone, crafted from red sandstone slabs.
entities.name: Chiseled Red Sandstone

entities.blurb: Chiseled resin bricks are a variant of resin bricks, crafted from resin brick slabs.
entities.name: Chiseled Resin Bricks

entities.blurb: Chiseled sandstone is a decorative variant of sandstone, crafted from sandstone slabs.
entities.name: Chiseled Sandstone

entities.blurb: Chiseled stone bricks are a variant of stone bricks, crafted from stone brick slabs.
entities.name: Chiseled Stone Bricks

entities.blurb: Chiseled sulfur is a decorative chiseled variant of sulfur used for building.
entities.name: Chiseled Sulfur
